animation_tooltip.exact_original: While a CPU-heavy job such as Measure runs, the animation pauses. While a GPU job such as mask generation runs, animations stop using the GPU. Your saved animation settings return when the jobs end. Off keeps animations running unchanged.
animation_tooltip.proposed: While a CPU-heavy job such as Measure runs, animated backdrops keep moving at up to 30 fps and Spaceout fractals pause. While a GPU job such as mask generation runs, decorative rendering uses the CPU and GPU-backed Spaceout fractals pause. Your saved animation settings return when the jobs end. Off disables this workload policy; other animation limits still apply.
reasons: Visible AmbientWidget backdrops remain animated during a run; _rate caps at min(configured fps, 30) when a pipeline or CPU workload paces them. This is a configured upper bound, not measured smoothness.
CPU-heavy jobs still pause Spaceout fractals; GPU jobs move decorative rendering to CPU and pause GPU-backed fractals. Avoid claiming every animation continues.
Dynamic animation off disables the workload policy, but pipeline responsiveness pacing and Reduce motion still apply; keep the wording from promising every saved rate is maintained.

AmbientWidget_stop.exact_original_docstring:
Stop ticking and retire the shading thread. Costs exactly nothing
while stopped — no timer, no thread, and no frame held in memory.

Dropping the published frame matters because these screens stay
built: a dozen module screens the user has visited would otherwise
each keep a slot warm behind a tab nobody is on, which is 2 MiB apiece
for the aurora. The next :meth:`start` shades a replacement before it
starts the thread, so there is nothing to show for it.

The one exception is a backdrop that stops while it is still on
screen -- a CPU-heavy run pausing the animation
(:func:`_animation_paused_for_work`), reduced motion, or the
animation switched off. Its frame on screen is kept as the still
(:meth:`_paint_still`), because every console line and figure the
window paints over it asks it for a whole frame again, and shading
that frame on the GUI thread against the run's worker took 250-350 ms
on lesson 08's Measure run. Hidden, it keeps nothing.

targeted_replace.replace:

targeted_replace.with:

targeted_replace.note: Re-read surrounding lifetime prose with Home before approval; old first paragraph says no held frame while stopped but later explicitly preserves a still when visible. This audit changes no docstring or runtime source.

proposed_changes.exact_original: Field backgrounds on Mask screens and in Spaceout draw more smoothly, at 60 fps. Ripples from a closed window run outward only, and the ripple slider scales waves up to 200 %.
proposed_changes.proposed: Field backgrounds on Mask screens and in Spaceout use a frame-rate cap of up to 60 fps. During analysis, animated backdrops are capped at up to 30 fps. Ripples from a closed window run outward only, and the ripple slider scales waves up to 200 %.
proposed_changes.why: Distinguishes configured caps from a promise of measured 60 fps. The cap follows display-aware idle rates and workload pacing; separate Spaceout fractals may pause. Ripple claims are unchanged and not independently performance-reviewed here.

source_basis.fact: auto field rate follows display refresh up to FIELD_FPS; _rate uses min(configured fps, _RUN_FPS)

proposed_changes.approval_dependency: Home confirms final app rates and actual capture gates; do not promise constant achieved 30/60 fps.

proposed_changes.exact_original: Preferences opens, applies and closes faster, and Apply, Keep and Revert no longer freeze the app.
proposed_changes.proposed: Preferences includes changes intended to reduce delays when opening, applying and closing.
proposed_changes.why: The blanket no-freeze statement is broader than the bound evidence. Historical accepted media contains a real Preferences Apply watchdog stall; no fresh final-app acceptance has been established by this advisory. Proposed wording states intent without claiming measured speedup or elimination of every stall.
proposed_changes.approval_dependency: Home should choose final wording after cold first Apply/Save and unchanged/nonvisual/scale variants have bound final-app evidence. If no public source change supports this intent, keep the bullet pending rather than claim it shipped.

proposed_changes.exact_original: The README is rebuilt from images, and the slide deck is rebuilt to match. README and interface text are translated into nine languages.
proposed_changes.proposed: The README is rebuilt from images, and the slide deck is rebuilt to match. README and interface localization catalogs are available in nine languages. Untranslated or stale entries fall back to English.
proposed_changes.why: Presence of nine catalogs is supported; broad completeness is not. The source-bound metadata audit still lists 20 missing and 20 stale API symbols per locale. Runtime metadata completeness alone is not a semantic translation acceptance.
proposed_changes.approval_dependency: Home confirms exact released language surfaces and fallback behavior before publication; README/deck claims otherwise remain unchanged and are not independently content-reviewed here.
